brief: Peter Callahan's Goldman TMT daily. NDX futures are down 30 bps in what he calls a holding pattern, the product of offsetting forces: datapoints are very supportive, citing DELL and NVDA results, volumes are anemic at roughly 20% below the year-to-date average yesterday, the macro backdrop is complicated ahead of a live FOMC meeting this month, and risk appetite is muted. Three stocks carry the note. MDB fell 14% as investors weigh stable Atlas growth near 29% year over year against the implied second-half outlook and whether EA upside comes at Atlas's expense. GIR stays BUY on record Atlas net adds of 2,900, Voyage customers nearly doubling for a second straight quarter, and self-hosted AI demand as an incremental growth vector. MDB trades about 30% below DDOG and SNOW on forward EV/Sales, which Callahan calls arguably valid because Atlas has yet to clear 30% growth. DELL rose 8% on back-to-back EPS beats above 40%, with ISG revenue up 89% against 75% guided and ISG margin at 15.0% versus GSe 11.7%, and raised its F2027 server and storage outlooks. GIR raised DELL EPS about 38% to roughly $30.53 in FY28. PANW slipped 1% on a headline beat and raise.
